content.text:
Lone surrogates no longer eat the next character, and all 1245 tests pass.

**Cause:** in the UTF-8 encoder in `lib/utils.js` (`encode`), any code unit from 0xD800 to 0xDFFF was assumed to be the high half of a surrogate pair. The encoder always took the next code unit as the low half without checking it. So `'\uD800x'` combined with the `x` into U+10078. A trailing high surrogate was combined with whatever came after the end of the string, which is the garbage in the second example.

**Fix:** a high surrogate is now combined only when the next code unit really is a low surrogate (0xDC00–0xDFFF). A lone high surrogate, or any low surrogate on its own, is encoded as `%EF%BF%BD` (U+FFFD) and the next character is encoded normally. Valid pairs encode exactly as before, including pairs split across the encoder's 1024-character chunk boundary.

I checked against `URLSearchParams` and the output matches for `'\uD800x'`, `'x\uDBFF'`, `'\uDC00 '`, a reversed pair, an emoji, and lone or valid pairs at the chunk boundary. The space case differs only in spacing style: qs writes `%20` where `URLSearchParams` writes `+`.

**Test changes:** two existing tests in `test/utils.js` asserted the old output: `'\uD83DX'` → `%F0%9F%91%98` (X dropped) and `'\uD83D \uDCA9'` → `%F0%9F%90%A0%F0%BA%90%80` (space dropped). They were the only failures after the fix, so I changed their expected values to the behaviour the bug report asks for. I also added tests for the cases in the report, a reversed pair, and an emoji.
